Japanese tennis player Kimiko Date-Krumm has apologised for the third time after her outburst at the US Open.

The 42-year-old was fined $10,000 (£6,400) for swearing at a lineswoman during her first-round defeat by Mandy Minella.

Date-Krumm, who was playing in her first Grand Slam since 1996, said she was "very sorry" for her behaviour.

"I was very upset and I was very angry," she said. "I'm very sorry for what I did."

Date-Krumm, who is ranked 120th in the world, was fined $2,000 for unsportsmanlike conduct and $8,000 for verbal abuse.
